gen-gf-bellota-gf-mandali: Bellota hangs its s ends wide and draws everything with one stylus. Mandali, in sans-serif dress, is the one that welcomes the eye into each e, while Bellota is the one that gets noticed first.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-manjari: Loose, stylus-drawn swagger up top. And Manjari, a sans-serif with wide unclosed curves and a steady line, takes over below, though shrinking Bellota would blunt the character that makes it stand out.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-meera-inimai: Meera Inimai has open-ended curves and a blueprint-lettering feel of constant line. Meera Inimai handles the quiet, practical work as a plain sans, while Bellota, with its far-hanging s ends, does the showing off.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-metrophobic: Rounded-nib charm up top, with diagonals as thick as horizontals and an s that hangs wide. Metrophobic, a sans, glides smoothly around each bend and handles the quiet work.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-mina: Bellota draws every stroke with one stylus, and its s ends drift well away from the spine. Mina, a sans with plain strokes and generously unclosed small round letters, does the steady, tidy work underneath.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-mingzat: Mingzat reads as a sans with curvy, unclamped letters that feel loose and easy. Mingzat would carry a long stretch of text gently, while Bellota's stout n arches stay at the top.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-moderustic: Broad-nib roundness, start to finish. Moderustic, a sans-serif, leaves its curves open like Bellota's unswelling stroke ends, and that shared unfinished, pen-drawn softness is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-molengo: Bellota is true monoline, every stroke traced with one stylus and its s ends flung far from the spine. Molengo, a plain sans, feels crisp and tidy beside it.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-momo-trust-sans: Chunky, friendly shapes all around. But Bellota's hanging s ends give the heading its flair, while Momo Trust Sans, a sans-serif with heavy bowls and open mouths, keeps the text approachable.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-mona-sans: Mona Sans opens its letters as wide as a door left ajar, which makes a plain sans feel welcoming. Bellota's constant pen pressure then gives the headings their character.
